summary: This note describes the hardware of the first-generation Amazon Kindle Fire tablet, which was manufactured by Quanta Computer. It covers the processor, the 7-inch multi-touch display, connectivity options, storage capacity, and battery life claims made by Amazon.
one_line: Hardware specifications of the first-generation Amazon Kindle Fire tablet, including its processor, display, storage and battery life.
key_facts: The Kindle Fire hardware was originally manufactured by Quanta Computer, an Original Design Manufacturer.
Quanta Computer had also helped design the BlackBerry PlayBook, which was used as a hardware template for the Kindle Fire.
First-generation Kindle Fire devices employed a 1 GHz Texas Instruments OMAP 4430 dual-core processor.
The Kindle Fire has a 2-point multi-touch color LCD screen with a diagonal length of 7 inches (180 mm).
The Kindle Fire's display has a 600 × 1024 pixel resolution with a density of 160 dpi.
The Kindle Fire connects via 802.11n Wi-Fi and USB 2.0 with a Micro-B connector.
The Kindle Fire includes 8 GB of internal storage.
Amazon said the 8 GB of internal storage is enough for 80 applications, plus either 10 movies or 800 songs or 6,000 books.
According to Amazon, the first-generation Kindle Fire has a 4400 mAh battery.
Amazon claims the first-generation Kindle Fire's battery sustains up to 8 hours of consecutive reading.
Amazon claims the first-generation Kindle Fire's battery sustains up to 7.5 hours of video playback with wireless off.
The note states that later Kindle Fire generations all offered battery life of around 7 to 8 hours.
